hero.eyebrow: Websites for small businesses and groups
hero.title: A website you own, and can talk to
hero.lede: We set up a website that lives in your own accounts, build it from your own documents and ideas, and teach you to change it by talking to Claude. Then we step back. No monthly fee, nothing held hostage.
points: Your domain, your repository, your AI account

how.title: How it works
how.intro: Five steps, each with a clear end. When the last one is done, the website is yours to run.

steps.name: Setup
steps.text: We help you open three accounts in your own name: an AI account (Claude, or ChatGPT if you prefer), a GitHub account with GitHub Pages, and a domain account. Then we connect Claude to your website's repository so it can make changes for you.
steps.detail: You hold every password. We are guests while we work.

steps.name: Build
steps.text: You send us what you already have: leaflets, price lists, old pages, photos, notes on the back of an envelope. We build the site from your own words and ideas, not from a template library.
steps.detail: As many pages as the material needs.

steps.name: Choose a design
steps.text: You get several design options built on your real content, not mock-ups with placeholder text. Pick one, or mix parts of two, and we carry it through the whole site.
steps.detail: Usually three directions to compare side by side.

steps.name: QA
steps.text: We go through rounds of checks with you: spelling, links, phones and tablets, how it reads aloud, what a stranger would understand. You note what is wrong; we fix it.
steps.detail: Rounds agreed up front, so you know when it ends.

steps.name: Handover
steps.text: A session where you change your own site by talking to Claude: add a page, update a price, swap an opening time. You leave knowing how to do it, and how to undo it.
steps.detail: After this you are in control, and we are not needed.

pay.title: What you pay
pay.intro: One-off packages. These prices are hypotheses for a demonstration: the market and the time the work takes will set the real ones.

packages.name: Simple site
packages.for: A handful of pages: who you are, what you do, where to find you.

packages.name: Larger site
packages.for: Catalogues, libraries of guides, events, many sections.
includes: Content structured as data, so pages are generated
Search or filtering where it helps

packages.name: Lift and shift
packages.unit: one-off, depends on the old back end
packages.for: An existing site you can no longer edit, moved into accounts you own.
includes: Copy of every page and file

extras.name: Domain for a year
extras.text: We can buy and set up the domain for you as a one-off, registered in your name. Renewal is yours to decide next year.

extras.name: Block of hours
extras.text: If you later want help, buy a block of hours. Only if you want it, used when you want it, and it runs out.

extras.name: No monthly fee
extras.text: Nothing recurring from us. Your own accounts may have their own costs, which you pay to them directly and can cancel.

own.title: What you own
own.intro: Three accounts, all in your name. Together they are the whole website.

accounts.name: Your AI account
accounts.text: The assistant you talk to. It is connected to your repository and makes the edits you ask for. Your conversations stay in your account.

accounts.name: Your GitHub account
accounts.text: Where the website lives: every page, picture and change, with a full history. GitHub Pages serves it to the world.

accounts.name: Your domain account
accounts.sub: DNS and the name people type
accounts.text: The address of your site. Registered to you, pointed at your GitHub Pages, renewed when you choose.

own.note: We hold nothing hostage: no logins only we know, no code only we can change, no hosting only we control.

why.title: Why no monthly fee
why.intro: Most small-business websites are rented. We think rent is the wrong shape for this work, for us as much as for you.

reasons.title: A monthly fee pays us when you don't use us
reasons.text: Most months a small site needs nothing. Rent turns those quiet months into money for doing nothing, and you notice.

reasons.title: The more you use it, the less we earn
reasons.text: On a flat fee, every request eats the margin. The incentive is to make changes feel slow and expensive. That is the opposite of what you want.

reasons.title: A few clients drive you mad
reasons.text: Any studio on retainers knows the pattern: a small number of clients take most of the hours. Everyone else pays for it, and the work gets worse.

reasons.title: So we sell finite engagements
reasons.text: Each piece of work has a start, a price and an end. It ends with you in control of your own site, able to change it by asking.

lift.title: Lift and shift
lift.intro: The person who built your website has left, the login is lost, or the system is so old nobody dares touch it. We move it to accounts you own.

steps.name: Copy
steps.text: We take a full copy of every page, image and document on the current site.

steps.name: Rebuild
steps.text: We rebuild it as a static site in your new GitHub repository, keeping the look or refreshing it.

steps.name: Redirect
steps.text: Old addresses keep working, so links in emails and search results still land.

steps.name: Switch
steps.text: We point your domain at the new site and check everything, then the old one can be switched off.

lift.pricing: £200 for a simple brochure site, up to £1,000 for an old content system with many pages. A hypothesis, set by how hard the old back end is to read.

examples.title: Three example sites
examples.intro: Three made-up clients in the made-up town of Harrowby. Each site was built the same way, and each looks different, because each client is different.

items.name: Tidewrack Studio Pottery
items.text: A filterable catalogue of mugs, bowls, vases and plates, generated from data. Classes, open studio days and a care guide. No checkout, by design.

items.name: Fennick Lane Community Garden
items.text: What they grow, plots and the waiting list, a season of events, a volunteer rota and a library of growing guides.

items.name: Quillon Heat & Plumbing
items.text: Services, areas covered, how to book, what to do in an emergency, and a library of household guides.

items.q: Is there a limit on pages?
items.a: No. The number of pages is limited only by what your own Claude account and your patience allow. A static site can hold tens, hundreds, even thousands of pages without trouble.

items.q: What if Claude gets it wrong?
items.a: GitHub keeps every version of every page. If a change looks wrong, ask Claude to undo it, or go back to any earlier version. Nothing is lost. We show you how in the handover.

items.q: What if I want help later?
items.a: Buy a block of hours. Use them when you want them. There is no subscription to cancel and nothing renews by itself.

items.q: Do I need to be technical?
items.a: No. If you can describe the change you want in a sentence, you can make it. The handover session is there so you try it with us beside you first.

items.q: What does it cost to run?
items.a: GitHub Pages is free for public sites. The domain renews yearly. Your AI account has its own plan, which you may already have. All three are paid by you, to them, and you can see every charge.
There is nothing to leave. Everything is already in your accounts. You can hire anyone, or nobody, from the day of the handover.

contact.title: Talk to us
contact.text: Kitewing is made up, so there is nobody to call. If this way of selling websites interests you, the article on newsroom.sgit.ai explains the thinking.
